commit.message:
Fix XDELEX/XACKDEL ACKED replying 2 for IDs not in the stream (#16243)

Fixes #16237

With `ACKED`, `XDELEX` and `XACKDEL` decide whether an entry is still
needed with `streamEntryIsReferenced()`. That function treats every ID
greater than the smallest last-delivered ID of the consumer groups as
referenced, whether or not such an entry exists, so both commands could
reply 2 for an ID that is not in the stream.

XDELEX, for an ID that was never added:

```
XADD mystream 1-0 f v
XGROUP CREATE mystream group1 0
XDELEX mystream KEEPREF IDS 1 5-0   -> -1
XDELEX mystream ACKED IDS 1 5-0     -> 2   (now -1)
```

XACKDEL, for an entry that was deleted while another group has not read
it:

```
XADD mystream 1-0 f v
XGROUP CREATE mystream g1 0
XGROUP CREATE mystream g2 0
XREADGROUP GROUP g1 c1 STREAMS mystream >
XDEL mystream 1-0
XACKDEL mystream g1 KEEPREF IDS 1 1-0   -> 1
XACKDEL mystream g1 ACKED IDS 1 1-0     -> 2   (now 1)
```

With this change, when `ACKED` keeps an entry, the reply is "still
referenced" only if the entry still exists in the stream:

- `XDELEX ... ACKED` replies -1 for an ID that is not in the stream, as
`KEEPREF` and `DELREF` do.
- `XACKDEL ... ACKED` replies 1 after acknowledging an entry that is no
longer in the stream. Other groups' pending references are kept.

---------

Signed-off-by: Dezhen Lu <dezhen.lu@student.uni-tuebingen.de>
Signed-off-by: 0z5a <dezhen.lu@student.uni-tuebingen.de>

files.patch:
@@ -1907,6 +1907,27 @@ start_server {
             assert_equal {0 {} {} {}} [r XPENDING mystream group2]
         }
 
+        test "XACKDEL with ACKED option replies 1 for acked entries that are no longer in the stream" {
+            r DEL mystream
+            r XADD mystream 1-0 f v
+            r XADD mystream 2-0 f v
+            r XGROUP CREATE mystream group1 0
+            r XGROUP CREATE mystream group2 0
+            r XREADGROUP GROUP group1 consumer1 STREAMS mystream >
+            r XREADGROUP GROUP group2 consumer2 COUNT 1 STREAMS mystream >
+
+            # Acknowledging either deleted entry succeeds even when another
+            # group still has a pending reference.
+            assert_equal 2 [r XDEL mystream 1-0 2-0]
+            assert_equal {1 1} [r XACKDEL mystream group1 ACKED IDS 2 1-0 2-0]
+            assert_equal {0 {} {} {}} [r XPENDING mystream group1]
+            assert_equal {1 1-0 1-0 {{consumer2 1}}} [r XPENDING mystream group2]
+
+            assert_equal {1} [r XACKDEL mystream group2 ACKED IDS 1 1-0]
+            assert_equal {0 {} {} {}} [r XPENDING mystream group2]
+            assert_equal 0 [r XLEN mystream]
+        }
+
         test "XGROUP CREATE with ENTRIESREAD larger than stream entries should cap the value" {
             r DEL mystream
             r xadd mystream * field value

@@ -4058,6 +4058,32 @@ start_server {tags {"stream"}} {
         assert_equal 0 [r XLEN mystream]
     }
 
+    test "XDELEX with ACKED option returns -1 for IDs that are not in the stream" {
+        r DEL mystream
+        r XADD mystream 1-0 f v
+        r XADD mystream 2-0 f v
+        r XGROUP CREATE mystream group1 0
+
+        # 5-0 was never added. It is past the last ID delivered to group1,
+        # but there is no entry to keep: the reply is -1, as without ACKED.
+        assert_equal {-1} [r XDELEX mystream KEEPREF IDS 1 5-0]
+        assert_equal {-1} [r XDELEX mystream ACKED IDS 1 5-0]
+
+        # The same for an entry that was deleted before any group read it.
+        assert_equal 1 [r XDEL mystream 2-0]
+        assert_equal {2 -1 -1} [r XDELEX mystream ACKED IDS 3 1-0 2-0 5-0]
+        assert_equal 1 [r XLEN mystream]
+
+        # A pending reference does not bring a deleted stream entry back.
+        r DEL mystream
+        r XADD mystream 1-0 f v
+        r XGROUP CREATE mystream group1 0
+        r XGROUP CREATE mystream group2 0
+        r XREADGROUP GROUP group1 consumer1 STREAMS mystream >
+        assert_equal 1 [r XDEL mystream 1-0]
+        assert_equal {-1} [r XDELEX mystream ACKED IDS 1 1-0]
+    }
+
     test "XDELEX with ACKED option won't delete messages when new consumer groups are created" {

         r XADD mystream 1-0 f v
